inflation may get worse before it gets better.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports on the latest findings

CEOs surveyed by the bank say, on average,
they expect to raise their prices by 3.7% over the next year.
That's a bigger price hike than executives were projecting six months ago,
but it's still not big enough to cover the higher costs
they expect their own companies to face.
CEOs project their costs will climb by more than 4%.
That's also up from the previous survey.
The Federal Reserve tries to limit inflation to just 2% per year,
but prices have been climbing faster than that for over five years now.
The central bank is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate next month
in an effort to tamp down demand and bring price hikes under control.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
